h: A Duke's Fancy and a Riverside Ramble
p: The Hermitage was created in the eighteenth century by the Dukes of Atholl as a romantic pleasure ground, designed to surprise and delight guests. Ossian's Hall was originally fitted out with mirrors and painted panels so the waterfall appeared to tumble all around visitors as they entered. Stand inside and look out through the viewing window for the full effect of the falls crashing below. Nearby, Ossian's Cave is a rough stone shelter built to look ancient, another bit of Georgian theatre.

If you've got more energy, the paths carry on upriver towards Rumbling Bridge, where the Braan squeezes through a narrow gorge. It turns a short stroll into a proper walk, but the scenery makes it worth it.

Allow around an hour for the short walk to the falls and back, or two to three hours if you go further. The car park can fill up quickly at weekends and in summer, so arrive early or late in the day for a calmer visit.

Dunkeld and its neighbour Birnam are packed with character. Dunkeld Cathedral, part ruined and part still in use, sits right on the banks of the Tay, and Birnam is linked to Beatrix Potter, who spent childhood holidays nearby, and to Shakespeare's Macbeth through the famous Birnam Wood. Wildlife lovers should head to the Loch of the Lowes reserve just outside town, which is known for its nesting ospreys in spring and summer. The Dunkeld and Birnam station is on the Highland line, so you can even leave the car at home.
